lessons.title: How to Use Alibaba, Made-in-China, and 1688
lessons.body: Alibaba is the world's largest B2B marketplace, with over 200,000 suppliers. For African importers, it's the go-to for small machines and pharmaceutical equipment. Start by searching for your product, e.g., 'tablet press machine' or 'packaging machine'. Use filters: 'Verified Supplier', 'Trade Assurance', and 'Ready to Ship' to narrow down. Alibaba shows prices in USD, but always ask for a quotation because listed prices are often outdated. Made-in-China.com is similar but often has more industrial suppliers and lower MOQs. 1688.com is Alibaba's domestic Chinese versionâprices are 20-30% lower, but you need a Chinese agent to buy and ship, as it doesn't export directly. For 1688, use a sourcing agent like Yoybuy or Superbuy; they charge 5-10% commission plus shipping. Always communicate via platform messaging, not WhatsApp or email, to keep records for disputes. For small machines, check the 'Transactions' and 'Reviews' sections. A supplier with 50+ transactions and 4.5+ rating is safer. Use Alibaba's 'Request for Quotation' (RFQ) tool: describe your needs, and within 24 hours you'll get 10-20 quotes. Compare prices, but don't choose the cheapestâlook for consistent pricing and detailed specs. For pharmaceuticals, ensure the supplier has GMP or ISO certificates. Always ask for a video call to see the factory. Remember: Alibaba is a directory, not a store. You're dealing with factories, not retailers. So negotiate. A 10% discount is common if you order 2+ units. Also, check shipping: Alibaba's 'Logistics' tab gives estimated freight to your port. For Nigeria, Lagos port; for Kenya, Mombasa. Use these tools to build a shortlist of 5-10 suppliers, then move to vetting.

lessons.title: Vetting Suppliers: Verified, Gold, and Trade Assurance
lessons.body: On Alibaba, 'Verified Supplier' means a third-party inspection company (like SGS or TÃV) has checked the company's license and factory. It's a good first filter, but it doesn't guarantee quality. 'Gold Supplier' is a paid membershipâit shows the supplier invested in marketing, not necessarily quality. Trade Assurance is your best protection: it's a free service where Alibaba holds your payment until you confirm receipt. If the goods don't match the contract, you can open a dispute and get a refund. Always insist on Trade Assurance for your first order. For Made-in-China, look for 'Audited Supplier' badges. For 1688, vetting is harderâuse an agent who can visit the factory. To vet deeply: ask for the business license (è¥ä¸æ§ç§) and check the registration number on China's National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (gsxt.gov.cn). The license shows registered capital, year established, and legal representative. A factory with 5+ years and 1M+ RMB capital is more stable. Next, request a live video tour via WeChat or WhatsApp. Ask to see the production line, warehouse, and testing equipment. If they refuse, walk away. Check for certifications: CE for machines, ISO 9001 for quality management, GMP for pharma equipment. Verify certificates by checking the issuing body's website. Also, search the supplier's name plus 'scam' or 'complaint' on Google. Use the Alibaba 'Company Profile' to see year established, total revenue, and main markets. A supplier with 10+ years and exports to Africa is a good sign. Finally, ask for 3 references from African buyers. If they hesitate, that's a red flag. Remember: vetting takes time, but it prevents losing thousands of dollars. For a $5,000 machine, spend at least 2 hours vetting. Use a checklist: license, video tour, certifications, references, and Trade Assurance. Only then proceed to samples.

lessons.title: Requesting Samples and Conducting Factory Audits
lessons.body: Always request a sample before placing a bulk order. For small machines, a sample might be a mini version or a component. For pharmaceuticals, it's a small batch of tablets or packaging. Expect to pay for the sample plus shippingâtypically $50-$200 for a small machine, $100-$300 for pharma samples. Never accept a free sample without paying shipping; it's often a scam. Ask for a 'sample invoice' via Trade Assurance. When the sample arrives, test it thoroughly: run it for 8 hours continuously, check output quality, and compare with specs. If it fails, negotiate improvements or find another supplier. For factory audits, you have two options: hire a third-party inspector (like QIMA, SGS, or Bureau Veritas) for $300-$500, or do it yourself via video call. A third-party audit gives a detailed report on production capacity, quality control, and working conditions. For a $10,000 order, it's worth it. If doing it yourself, schedule a video call during working hours (China time). Ask to see: raw materials, production line, assembly, testing, and packaging. Request live footage, not pre-recorded. Ask the factory manager to show you the QC logbook. For pharma, check for clean rooms and sterilization equipment. After the audit, ask for a 'factory audit report' if third-party. If you can't travel, consider using a local agent in China (e.g., from Freightos or Sourcify) to visit for $100-$200. Always document everything: photos, videos, and notes. If the supplier refuses an audit, that's a major red flag. Remember: a sample is your first quality check, and an audit is your second. Both are essential for high-value orders. For small machines under $1,000, a sample may suffice. For orders above $5,000, insist on an audit.

lessons.title: Understanding MOQs, FOB, and CIF Pricing
lessons.body: MOQ stands for Minimum Order Quantity. It's the smallest number of units a supplier will sell. For small machines, MOQs range from 1 to 10 units. For pharmaceuticals, MOQs can be 1,000 to 10,000 tablets. Always negotiate MOQâmany suppliers will lower it for a higher price per unit. For example, if MOQ is 5 units at $500 each, you might get 2 units at $600 each. FOB (Free On Board) means the supplier delivers goods to the port in China (e.g., Shanghai, Shenzhen) and loads them onto the ship. You pay for freight, insurance, and import duties. CIF (Cost, Insurance, Freight) means the supplier pays for shipping and insurance to your port (e.g., Lagos, Mombasa). CIF is easier for beginners but often 10-20% more expensive. For a $5,000 machine, FOB might be $5,000 + $800 freight = $5,800; CIF might be $6,200. Always get both quotes. For Africa, sea freight takes 30-45 days from China to West Africa, 20-30 days to East Africa. Air freight is faster (5-7 days) but 5-10 times more expensiveâonly for urgent, high-value items. When comparing quotes, ensure they specify: FOB port, shipping line, transit time, and destination port. Also, check if the price includes export clearance and local charges. For pharmaceuticals, ensure the supplier provides a Certificate of Analysis (COA) and MSDS. Always ask for a proforma invoice (PI) that details: unit price, MOQ, total price, FOB/CIF terms, payment terms, and delivery time. Compare at least 3 PIs. Remember: the cheapest FOB price might not be the best if the supplier is far from the port (extra inland freight). Use a freight forwarder to get the best rates. For small machines, a 20ft container can hold 10-20 units; a 40ft container 20-40 units. Consolidate orders to save on freight.

lessons.title: Payment Methods: T/T, Letters of Credit, Escrow
lessons.body: T/T (Telegraphic Transfer) is a bank wire transfer. It's the most common payment method for Chinese suppliers. Typically, you pay 30% deposit, then 70% before shipping. For a $5,000 order, that's $1,500 deposit and $3,500 before shipment. T/T is fast (1-3 days) but risky if the supplier disappears. Only use T/T with Trade Assurance or a trusted supplier. L/C (Letter of Credit) is a bank guarantee. Your bank pays the supplier only when shipping documents are presented. It's safer for large orders (above $10,000) but expensive: banks charge 1-3% of the order value, plus document fees. L/C requires precise documentsâany discrepancy can delay payment. For African importers, L/C is common for orders above $20,000. Escrow (like Alibaba's Trade Assurance) is the safest: Alibaba holds your payment until you confirm receipt. It's free and protects both parties. For first orders, always use Escrow. For repeat orders, T/T with a 30% deposit is acceptable if you trust the supplier. Other methods: Western Union and MoneyGram are fast but have no protectionânever use them for business. PayPal is safe but expensive (4-5% fees) and rarely accepted by Chinese factories. For pharmaceuticals, some suppliers accept payment via Alipay or WeChat Pay, but these are hard for foreigners. Always pay to a company bank account, not a personal one. Check the beneficiary name matches the company name on the PI. For T/T, use your bank's online portal; fees are $20-$50. For L/C, work with your bank's trade finance department. Never pay 100% upfront. If a supplier insists, walk away. For orders above $50,000, consider using a trade finance company like Trefis or Stenn. Remember: payment terms are negotiable. A good supplier will accept 30/70. A scammer will demand 100% T/T.

lessons.title: Avoiding Scams and Rogue Traders
lessons.body: Scams are common in Chinese sourcing. The most common: fake suppliers who take your deposit and disappear. To avoid: never pay to a personal account. Always pay to a company account with the same name as the supplier on Alibaba. Check the bank account's countryâit should be in China. If it's in Hong Kong or another country, be suspicious. Second scam: quality switch. They send a good sample, then ship inferior goods. Prevent this by using Trade Assurance and specifying quality in the contract. Third scam: fake certificates. Always verify certificates on the issuing body's website. For CE, check the EU's NANDO database. For ISO, check the issuing body's site. Fourth scam: hidden fees. They quote a low FOB price, then add charges for packaging, documentation, or inland freight. Always ask for a full quotation with all costs. Fifth scam: fake reviews. On Alibaba, check the 'Transactions' tabâif a supplier has many transactions but no reviews, be wary. Use Google to search the supplier's name plus 'scam' or 'fraud'. Also, check the Alibaba 'Blacklist' forum. For pharmaceuticals, beware of suppliers selling unregistered drugs. Always ask for a drug registration certificate from China's NMPA. If they can't provide, walk away. Red flags: poor English, evasive answers, pressure to pay quickly, prices too low, no physical address, no landline. Use a sourcing agent for high-value ordersâthey charge 5-10% but can verify the supplier. For small machines under $2,000, use Trade Assurance and a sample. For orders above $10,000, hire a third-party inspector. If you get scammed, report to Alibaba and your local police. Also, file a complaint with China's Ministry of Commerce. Remember: if it sounds too good to be true, it is. Always trust your gut. A legitimate supplier will answer all questions and provide documents. A scammer will rush you.

lessons.title: Practical Reference
lessons.body:
Practical Reference: Sourcing Machinery from China

This practical reference lesson consolidates the operational knowledge you need to source small machines and pharmaceutical equipment from China with confidence. It covers platform selection, supplier vetting, sampling and audits, pricing terms, payment methods, and scam avoidance â all tailored to African importers moving goods into Lagos, Mombasa, Tema, Durban, or Djibouti. Treat this as your desk-side manual: when a supplier sends a quotation, you should be able to cross-check every number and every claim against the frameworks below.

China remains Africa's largest single source of machinery and pharmaceutical inputs. According to UN Comtrade data, China accounted for roughly 16â18% of Africa's total merchandise imports in recent years, with machinery and electrical equipment among the top categories. For small-scale manufacturers â water bottlers, feed millers, soap and detergent producers, tablet and capsule packagers â Chinese suppliers offer the widest range at the most competitive price points. The risk is not the country; it is the specific supplier. This lesson gives you the tools to separate the serious manufacturers from the traders and the outright fraudsters.

Platform Selection: Alibaba, Made-in-China, and 1688

Each platform serves a different purpose and a different risk profile. Alibaba is the most accessible for African buyers: English interface, Trade Assurance escrow, and a large pool of exporters accustomed to international shipping. Made-in-China tends to attract heavier industrial suppliers and verified manufacturers, often with more technical documentation. 1688 is China's domestic wholesale platform â prices are typically 20â40% lower than Alibaba, but the interface is in Chinese, suppliers rarely export directly, and you almost always need a sourcing agent or freight forwarder with a Chinese entity to buy and consolidate.

Vetting Suppliers: Verified, Gold, and Trade Assurance

Alibaba's badges are useful but frequently misunderstood. "Verified Supplier" means a third-party inspection company (often SGS, TÃV, or Bureau Veritas) has confirmed the company's legal existence and basic premises â it does not guarantee product quality. "Gold Supplier" is a paid membership tier; it signals willingness to invest in the platform, not manufacturing capability. "Trade Assurance" is the most valuable: it is an escrow-style protection where payment is held until you confirm the order meets the agreed specification. Always insist on Trade Assurance orders for first purchases, and always pay through the platform, never by direct bank transfer to a supplier's personal account.

Beyond badges, verify the business licence (ç»ä¸ç¤¾ä¼ä¿¡ç¨ä»£ç  â the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code) on China's National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (gsxt.gov.cn). Cross-check the company name on the licence against the bank account name on the proforma invoice. If they differ, stop.

Table 1: Platform comparison for African importers
Feature Alibaba Made-in-China 1688
LanguageEnglishEnglishChinese only
Escrow protectionTrade AssuranceLimitedNone (domestic)
Typical price level$$$$$
Export experienceHighHighLow
Agent requiredNoNoYes
Best forFirst-time buyersIndustrial machineryRepeat buyers with agent

Source: Alibaba.com Supplier Membership Terms; Made-in-China.com Buyer Guide; 1688.com platform documentation. Compiled by RISE AFRICA Skills, 2024.

Requesting Samples and Conducting Factory Audits

Never place a production order without a physical sample in your hand â or at minimum, a video-verified sample tested by a third party. Request the sample be shipped by express courier (DHL, FedEx) to your address, and pay for it. A supplier who refuses to send a sample, or who sends a sample that differs from the quoted specification, is a supplier you walk away from.

For orders above USD 5,000, commission a pre-shipment inspection (PSI). SGS, Bureau Veritas, Intertek, and QIMA all operate in China and can inspect at the factory for USD 300â800 depending on scope. For pharmaceutical equipment, insist on a GMP-readiness check and verify any CE, ISO 9001, or ISO 13485 certificates directly with the issuing body â not just the PDF the supplier sends.

Understanding MOQs, FOB, and CIF Pricing

MOQ (Minimum Order Quantity) is the smallest order a factory will accept. For small machines, MOQs are often 1 unit; for pharmaceutical packaging materials, MOQs can be 10,000+ units. Negotiate MOQ only after you have confirmed the unit price â suppliers sometimes lower MOQ but raise price.

FOB (Free On Board) means the supplier delivers to the named Chinese port and you pay freight and insurance from there. CIF (Cost, Insurance, Freight) means the supplier arranges freight and insurance to your destination port. CIF looks simpler but hides margin â always ask for both FOB and CIF quotes and compare, because the difference tells you the true freight cost.

Table 2: Incoterms and payment methods â risk allocation
Term / Method Who arranges freight Who bears risk in transit Best used when
FOB Shanghai/NingboBuyerBuyer after loadingYou have a freight forwarder
CIF Mombasa/LagosSupplierSupplier to destination portFirst shipment, no forwarder
T/T 30% deposit, 70% before shipmentâBuyer exposed on depositEstablished supplier, small order
Letter of Credit (L/C)âBank mitigatesOrders above USD 20,000
Trade Assurance / EscrowâPlatform holds fundsNew supplier, any size

Source: International Chamber of Commerce Incoterms 2020; International Trade Centre Trade Finance Guide (2022); Alibaba Trade Assurance Terms.

Payment Methods: T/T, Letters of Credit, Escrow

Telegraphic Transfer (T/T) is the most common method for AfricanâChina trade. A typical structure is 30% deposit, 70% before shipment. This is workable with a trusted supplier but exposes you if the supplier disappears after the deposit. For orders above USD 20,000, use a Letter of Credit (L/C) â your bank pays only against compliant shipping documents, which protects both sides. For new suppliers, use Trade Assurance or a similar escrow so funds are released only after you confirm receipt and inspection.

â  RED SAFETY WARNING â Scam Avoidance

Never pay a Chinese supplier by Western Union, MoneyGram, or direct transfer to a personal bank account. These are the three most common vectors for advance-fee fraud targeting African importers. Always pay to a company account whose name matches the business licence exactly. If a "supplier" claims to be a factory but cannot provide a business licence, factory address, or verifiable export history, treat it as a trader or fraudster. If the price is 40% or more below the market average, it is almost certainly a bait-and-switch or non-delivery scam. When in doubt, walk away â there are thousands of legitimate Chinese suppliers.

Quick Reference Checklist

  1. Define your specification in writing â capacity, voltage (Africa: 220â240V, 50Hz), certification required (CE, ISO, GMP for pharma), and packaging.
  2. Verify the business licence on gsxt.gov.cn and confirm the bank account name matches the licence exactly.
  3. Use Trade Assurance or escrow for first orders with any new supplier, regardless of order size.
  4. Order a paid sample and test it before committing to production; never accept a "free" sample that you cannot inspect independently.
  5. Commission a pre-shipment inspection (SGS, BV, Intertek, QIMA) for orders above USD 5,000.
  6. Request both FOB and CIF quotes and compare the freight component before choosing.
  7. Use L/C for orders above USD 20,000; use T/T only with an established, verified supplier.
  8. Never pay by Western Union, MoneyGram, or personal account â these are the primary scam vectors.

Further Reading

  • US International Trade Administration â China Import Requirements and Documentation (free official guide).
  • International Trade Centre â Sourcing and Trade Finance publications (free downloads).
  • ICC Incoterms 2020 â official rules reference.
  • China National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (gsxt.gov.cn) â verify any Chinese company's licence.
  • WTO World Trade Report â global trade and developing-country integration (free PDF).

Compiled by RISE AFRICA Skills for the course Small Machines & Pharmaceuticals: The Complete Import Business. Module: Sourcing Machinery from China. Data current as of 2024. Always verify supplier credentials and current regulations with official sources before committing funds.

quiz.q: Which platform is Alibaba's domestic Chinese version with lower prices but requires an agent?
quiz.explanation: 1688.com is Alibaba's domestic site, offering lower prices but not direct export, so an agent is needed.

quiz.q: What does 'Trade Assurance' on Alibaba do?
options: B) Holds payment until you confirm receipt
quiz.explanation: Trade Assurance holds your payment in escrow until you confirm the goods meet the contract.

quiz.q: Which badge on Alibaba indicates a third-party inspection of the company's license and factory?
quiz.explanation: Verified Supplier means a third-party like SGS has checked the company's license and factory.

quiz.q: What is the best way to verify a Chinese supplier's business license?
quiz.explanation: China's National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (gsxt.gov.cn) allows you to verify the license number.

quiz.q: What should you do if a supplier refuses a video factory tour?
quiz.explanation: Refusal to show the factory live is a major red flag and suggests they may not be legitimate.

quiz.q: What is a typical cost for a third-party factory audit?
quiz.explanation: Companies like QIMA or SGS charge around $300-$500 for a detailed factory audit.

quiz.q: When testing a sample machine, how long should you run it continuously?
quiz.explanation: Running for 8 hours helps identify overheating, breakdowns, or quality issues.

quiz.q: What does MOQ stand for?
quiz.explanation: MOQ is the smallest number of units a supplier will sell.

quiz.q: In FOB terms, who pays for the freight from China to your port?
quiz.explanation: FOB means the supplier delivers to the Chinese port, and the buyer pays for freight and insurance.

quiz.q: Which is typically more expensive for the buyer: FOB or CIF?
quiz.explanation: CIF includes shipping and insurance, so it's usually 10-20% higher than FOB.

quiz.q: How long does sea freight take from China to West Africa?
quiz.explanation: Sea freight to West Africa typically takes 30-45 days.

quiz.q: What document should you always request from a supplier before payment?
quiz.explanation: A proforma invoice details the order, terms, and payment instructions, serving as a contract.

quiz.q: What is the safest payment method for a first order with a new supplier?
quiz.explanation: Trade Assurance holds payment until you confirm receipt, protecting both parties.

quiz.q: In a typical T/T payment, what percentage is usually paid as deposit?
quiz.explanation: A 30% deposit is standard, with 70% before shipping.

quiz.q: Which payment method is a bank guarantee that pays only upon presentation of shipping documents?
quiz.explanation: A Letter of Credit (L/C) is a bank guarantee that requires compliant documents for payment.

quiz.q: What is a major risk of using Western Union for business payments?
quiz.explanation: Western Union offers no buyer protection, so it's unsafe for business transactions.

quiz.q: When paying via T/T, the beneficiary name should match:
options: B) The company name on the PI
quiz.explanation: Always ensure the bank account name matches the supplier's company name to avoid fraud.

quiz.q: What is a common scam in Chinese sourcing?
options: A) Sending a better sample than the bulk order
quiz.explanation: A quality switch scam involves sending a good sample but shipping inferior goods.

quiz.q: How can you verify a CE certificate?
options: A) Check the EU's NANDO database
quiz.explanation: The NANDO database lists valid CE certificates and notified bodies.

quiz.q: What should you do if a supplier demands 100% T/T upfront?
quiz.explanation: Demanding 100% upfront is a major red flag; legitimate suppliers accept a deposit.

quiz.q: Which of these is a red flag for a scam supplier?
options: C) Pressures you to pay quickly
quiz.explanation: High-pressure sales tactics are common in scams; legitimate suppliers are patient.

quiz.q: What is the best way to check a supplier's reputation?
quiz.explanation: Using multiple methods gives a fuller picture of the supplier's reliability.

quiz.q: For pharmaceutical equipment, which certification is essential?
quiz.explanation: GMP (Good Manufacturing Practice) is critical for pharmaceutical equipment.

quiz.q: What does a 'Gold Supplier' badge on Alibaba indicate?
quiz.explanation: Gold Supplier is a paid membership, not a guarantee of quality.

quiz.q: When comparing FOB and CIF quotes, what should you check?
options: B) Shipping line and transit time
quiz.explanation: FOB and CIF quotes should specify shipping line and transit time to compare fairly.

quiz.q: What is a proforma invoice used for?
quiz.explanation: A proforma invoice outlines the order details, terms, and payment instructions.

quiz.q: Which payment method is free and protects both buyer and seller on Alibaba?
quiz.explanation: Trade Assurance is free and holds payment until both parties are satisfied.

quiz.q: What is the first step in vetting a supplier?
quiz.explanation: Verifying the business license confirms the company's legal existence and details.

quiz.q: What should you do if a supplier's bank account is in Hong Kong but the company is in mainland China?
quiz.explanation: A mismatch in country is a red flag; verify the account's legitimacy before paying.

quiz.q: What is the typical commission for a sourcing agent in China?
quiz.explanation: Sourcing agents usually charge 5-10% of the order value for their services.
